items.title: Definition 7.1.1 (2017: 7.1): groupoids, $\mathrm{mor}(x, y)$ and the orbit space $|X|$

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.1 (2017: 7.1) and the paragraph after it, pp. 287–288 (2017 pp. 225–226)
book.statement:
A *groupoid* $X = (X, \mathbf X)$ is a small category consisting of the set $X$ of objects, denoted by $x$, and the set $\mathbf X$ of morphisms (arrows), which are assumed to be invertible, and the following five structure maps $(s, t, m, u, \iota)$. (1) The source and target maps $s, t : \mathbf X \to X$ assign to every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ in $\mathbf X$ its source $s(\varphi) = x$ and its target $t(\varphi) = y$. (2) The associative multiplication (composition) map $m : \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X \to \mathbf X$, $m(\varphi, \psi) = \varphi \circ \psi$, is defined on the fibered product $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X = \{(\varphi, \psi) \in \mathbf X \times \mathbf X \mid s(\varphi) = t(\psi)\}$, so that if $\psi : x \to z$ and $\varphi : z \to y$, then $\varphi \circ \psi : x \to y$. (3) For every object $x \in X$ there exists the unit morphism $1_x : x \to x$ in $\mathbf X$, a 2-sided unit for the composition: $\varphi \circ 1_x = \varphi$ and $1_x \circ \psi = \psi$ for all $\varphi, \psi \in \mathbf X$ satisfying $s(\varphi) = x = t(\psi)$; these define the unit map $u : X \to \mathbf X$, $u(x) = 1_x$. (4) For every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ there exists the inverse morphism $\varphi^{-1} : y \to x$, a 2-sided inverse: $\varphi \circ \varphi^{-1} = 1_y$ and $\varphi^{-1} \circ \varphi = 1_x$; these define the inverse map $\iota : \mathbf X \to \mathbf X$, $\iota(\varphi) = \varphi^{-1}$.

After the definition: $\mathrm{mor}(x, y) \subset \mathbf X$ is the set of all morphisms $\varphi$ with $s(\varphi) = x$ and $t(\varphi) = y$. The *orbit space* $|X| = X/\sim$ is the quotient of the set of objects by the equivalence relation $x \sim y$ if and only if there exists a morphism $\varphi : x \to y$; the class of $x$ is $|x| := \{y \in X \mid y \sim x\}$, and $\pi : X \to |X|$, $\pi(x) = |x|$, is the quotient map.

book.statement: For fixed $x \in X$ we denote by $G_x$ the isotropy group (stabilizer group) of $x$, defined by $G_x = \{\varphi \in \mathbf X \mid \varphi : x \to x\}$.

items.title: Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3): ep-groupoids

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3), pp. 288 ff. (2017 pp. 226–227)
book.statement: An *ep-groupoid* $X = (X, \mathbf X)$ consists of a groupoid equipped with M-polyfold structures on the object set $X$ and the morphism set $\mathbf X$ having the following properties. (1) (étale) The source and target maps $s, t : \mathbf X \to X$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms. (2) The unit map $u$ and the inverse map $\iota$ are sc-smooth. (3) (Properness) Every point $x \in X$ possesses an open neighborhood $V(x)$ of $x$ in $X$ such that the map $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))) \to X$ is proper. Since $s$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism, the fibered product $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X$ is in a natural way an M-polyfold in view of Lemma 2.8 in [38], and we require (4) the multiplication map $m : \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X \to \mathbf X$ is sc-smooth. In particular, all the structure maps $(s, t, m, u, \iota)$ are sc-smooth maps.

lean.statement: `EpGroupoid Obj Mor` extends `GroupoidStr` by M-polyfold structures `PObj`, `PMor` on the Hausdorff paracompact spaces $X$, $\mathbf X$ and the conditions (1) `isLocalScDiffeo_src`, `isLocalScDiffeo_tgt`; (2) `isScSmoothMap_unit`, `isScSmoothMap_inv`; (3) `exists_isProperMap`: every $x$ has an open $V \ni x$ such that $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}\,V) \to X$ is a proper map (Mathlib's `IsProperMap` of the restriction); (4) `isScSmoothComp`, i.e. `IsScSmoothComp`: $m$ is sc-smooth on $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X$ with the sub-M-polyfold structure of Part I (`MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_fibredProduct`). (4) is equivalent to the sheet form `IsScSmoothCompSheet`: for every sheet $\sigma$ of $s$ over $V$, $\psi \mapsto m(\sigma(t(\psi)), \psi)$ is sc-smooth on $t^{-1}(V)$ (`isScSmoothComp_iff_sheet`, `EpGroupoid.isScSmoothCompSheet`); $s$ and $t$ are sc-smooth (`isScSmoothMap_src`, `isScSmoothMap_tgt`).

items.title: Properness and its sequential form

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.3 (3) (2017: 7.3), 2017 p. 227; used on pp. 292–346 (2017 pp. 230–254)
book.statement: Definition 7.1.3 (3) (2017: 7.3) asks that $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))) \to X$ be proper. The proofs use this in the form: if $s(\varphi_k) \in \mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))$ and $t(\varphi_k)$ converges in $X$, then, "after perhaps taking a subsequence", $(\varphi_k)$ converges in $\mathbf X$ (Proposition 7.1.10 (2017: 7.3), 2017 p. 230; Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1), p. 292 (2017 p. 230); Proposition 7.1.22 (2017: 7.7), p. 307 (2017 p. 238); Proposition 7.3.9 (2017: 7.11), 2017 p. 248; Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8), 2017 p. 254), or through the compactness of preimages of compact sets (Proposition 7.5.9 (2017: 7.13), p. 342 (2017 p. 251)). After Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4) (p. 289 (2017 p. 227)) the text points out that this properness differs from that of classical Lie groupoids, which requires $(s, t) : \mathbf X \to X \times X$ to be proper, a requirement too weak for some of the constructions.

items.title: Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4): the local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$ and the tangent $T\varphi$

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4) and the paragraph before it, 2017 p. 227
book.statement: Since $s, t : \mathbf X \to X$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms, every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ of an ep-groupoid has an extension to a local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$ satisfying $\hat\varphi(x) = y$, defined as follows: there exist open neighborhoods $\mathbf U(\varphi) \subset \mathbf X$ and $U(x), U(y) \subset X$ such that $s : \mathbf U(\varphi) \to U(x)$ and $t : \mathbf U(\varphi) \to U(y)$ are sc-diffeomorphisms, and $\hat\varphi = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1} : U(x) \to U(y)$. In the case that $\varphi$ is smooth, i.e. $\varphi \in \mathbf X_\infty$, there is an associated sc-isomorphism $T\varphi : T_{s(\varphi)}X \to T_{t(\varphi)}X$ defined by $T\varphi := T\hat\varphi(x)$; more generally $T\hat\varphi : TU(s(\varphi)) \to TU(t(\varphi))$. $T\varphi$ can be defined for $\varphi$ on level at least $1$ and gives a bounded linear isomorphism on level $0$; only in the case that $\varphi$ is smooth is $T\varphi$ an sc-operator. Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4): associated to a smooth morphism $\varphi$ we have the so-called associated local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$, as well as its tangent $T\varphi$.

items.title: The levels of an ep-groupoid and the filtration of $|X|$

book.label: §7.1, pp. 289–291 (2017 pp. 227–228)
book.statement: The M-polyfolds $X$ and $\mathbf X$ are equipped with the filtrations $X = X_0 \supset X_1 \supset X_2 \supset \dots \supset X_\infty = \bigcap_{k \ge 0} X_k$ and similarly for $\mathbf X$; $X_\infty$ is dense in every $X_k$. For $x$ in the M-polyfold $X$, $ml(x) \in \mathbb N \cup \{\infty\}$ is the largest non-negative integer $m$, or $\infty$, such that $x \in X_m$. Since the source and target maps are local sc-diffeomorphisms and therefore preserve the levels, $ml(x) = ml(y) = ml(\varphi)$ for every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$; consequently the filtration of $X$ induces the filtration $|X| = |X_0| \supset |X_1| \supset \dots \supset |X_\infty| = \bigcap_{k \ge 0}|X_k|$ of the orbit space. The degeneracy indices $d_X : X \to \mathbb N$ and $d_{\mathbf X} : \mathbf X \to \mathbb N$ are invariant under local sc-diffeomorphisms (Proposition 2.4.4 (2017: 2.7)), so $d_X(s(\varphi)) = d_{\mathbf X}(\varphi) = d_X(t(\varphi))$ for every morphism $\varphi$; in particular $d_X(x) = d_X(x')$ if $x \sim x'$.

Added: $|X_\infty|$ is dense in $|X|$ (`dense_orbitSmooth`).

items.title: Definition 7.1.6 (2017: 7.6): tame ep-groupoids; $\mathbf X$ is then tame

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.6 (2017: 7.6) and the paragraph after it, 2017 p. 228
book.statement: The ep-groupoid $(X, \mathbf X)$ is called *tame* if the object space $X$ is a tame M-polyfold as introduced in Definition 2.5.7 (2017: 2.19). In a tame ep-groupoid not only $X$ is a tame M-polyfold but also $\mathbf X$ is a tame M-polyfold. This follows from the facts that $\mathbf X$ is locally sc-diffeomorphic by $s$ to $X$ and the tameness condition is invariant under local sc-diffeomorphisms.

lean.statement: `EpGroupoid.IsTame` is `MPolyfold.IsTame` of the object M-polyfold: an equivalent atlas of charts modelled on tame retracts exists (Definition 2.5.7 (2017: 2.19)). A chart is transported along an sc-diffeomorphism to a tame chart (`MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn.exists_tame_chart`), so the domain of a local sc-diffeomorphism into a tame M-polyfold is tame (`MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isTame`), and for surjective ones the domain is tame iff the target is (`MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isTame_iff_of_surjective`); applied to $s$, this is the tameness of $\mathbf X$.

items.title: The remark after Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7): sc-smoothness on objects suffices

book.label: §7.1, after Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7), pp. 290 ff. (2017 pp. 228–229)
book.statement: It is sufficient to require that the functor $f$ is sc-smooth between the object spaces $X \to Y$, because the sc-smoothness of $f : \mathbf X \to \mathbf Y$ follows from the properties of the source map $s : \mathbf X \to X$: given $\varphi \in \mathbf X$ and $f(\varphi) = \psi \in \mathbf Y$ there exist open neighborhoods $\mathbf U(\varphi)$, $\mathbf U(\psi)$, $U(s(\varphi))$ and $U(s(\psi))$ satisfying $f(U(s(\varphi))) \subset U(s(\psi))$ and $f(\mathbf U(\varphi)) \subset \mathbf U(\psi)$; moreover, $s : \mathbf U(\varphi) \to U(s(\varphi))$ and $s : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(s(\psi))$ are sc-diffeomorphisms. Therefore the claim follows from the formula $f(\gamma) = (s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}(f(s(\gamma)))$ for all $\gamma \in \mathbf U(\varphi)$.

items.title: The quotient topology of $|X|$ and Proposition 7.1.8 (2017: 7.1): $\pi$ is open

book.label: §7.1, Proposition 7.1.8 (2017: 7.1) and the paragraph before it, 2017 p. 229
book.statement: The orbit space $|X|$ is equipped with the quotient topology, the finest topology for which the projection $\pi : X \to |X|$, $x \mapsto |x|$, is continuous: a subset $V$ of $|X|$ is open if and only if $\pi^{-1}(V)$ is open in $X$. Proposition 7.1.8 (2017: 7.1) (Openness of $\pi$): Let $(X, \mathbf X)$ be an ep-groupoid and assume that the orbit space $|X|$ is equipped with the quotient topology. Then the projection map $\pi : X \to |X|$ is open.

items.title: Proposition 7.1.9 (2017: 7.2): countable neighbourhood bases of $|X|$

book.statement: For a tame ep-groupoid: (1) $bX$ and $b\mathbf X$ have natural metrizable topologies; (2) natural tame M-polyfold structures; (3) both maps $B$ are sc-smooth; (4) $d_X(B(p)) - 1 = d_{bX}(p)$, and likewise on $b\mathbf X$; (5) $(bX, b\mathbf X)$ with $s, t, u, \iota, m$ is a tame ep-groupoid. The topology and the structure are characterized as in Theorem 2.7.13.

lean.statement: `theorem_7_6_9_full` (for `X.IsTame`): (1) metrizable $bX$, $b\mathbf X$; (2) `bPObj`, `bPMor` tame, and for every triple with $V$ centred at $x$, `uSet` open and `phiTot` an sc-diffeomorphism onto `facePolyfold` with inverse `phiHomeomorph.symm`, and every M-polyfold structure with this property has an atlas equivalent to `bPObj`, resp. `bPMor`; (3) both `tameBoundaryMap` sc-smooth; (4) $d_X(B p) - 1 = d_{bX}(p)$, $d_{\mathbf X}(B a) - 1 = d_{b\mathbf X}(a)$; (5) `boundaryEpGroupoid` tame, with the groupoid `boundaryGroupoid` and the structures `bPObj`, `bPMor`, local sc-diffeomorphisms `bSrc`, `bTgt`, sc-smooth `bUnit`, `bInv`, `IsScSmoothComp`; an `EpFunctor` with object and morphism maps the two `tameBoundaryMap`. Witness: `trivial_quadrant_boundaryEp_witness` ($[0, \infty)^n \oplus W$, $n \ge 1$: tame, nonempty $bX$, $b\mathbf X$, $d_{bX} = n - 1$ over the corner). For every representative $t$ of $bX$ and of $b\mathbf X$, centred or not: `theorem_7_6_9_allReps` ($\Phi_t$ an sc-diffeomorphism from `uSet t` onto the open `reachSet t`, which is $\theta$ for centred $V$, and uniqueness of the structures).

items.title: Proposition 7.4.9, and Corollary 7.4.11, Theorems 7.4.13, 7.4.24 for every $X^i$: (ZHOU) passes to every $X^i$

items.title: Proposition 7.4.18: (VSLUC) and (SLUC) are equivalent

book.label: §7.4, Proposition 7.4.18, p. 336 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: (VSLUC) and (SLUC) are equivalent. The proof of (SLUC) ⇒ (VSLUC) takes $V(x) = U(x) \cap X_\infty$ and uses that an open subset of it contains $W' \cap X_\infty$ for an open $W'$ of some $X_N$, with $U(x) \cap X_N$ connected by construction.

The forms first proved, with `DenseSmooth`, `SmoothConnected` for every $X^i$ and level-connected representations as hypotheses, are kept (`EP.eqOn_of_level_smooth`, `EP.isVSLUC_of_isSLUC`, `EP.proposition_7_4_18`). notFormalized.title: Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4): the tangent $T\varphi$ as an sc-isomorphism
notFormalized.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4) and the paragraph before it, 2017 p. 227
notFormalized.book: For a smooth morphism $\varphi$, i.e. $\varphi \in \mathbf X_\infty$, there is an associated sc-isomorphism $T\varphi : T_{s(\varphi)}X \to T_{t(\varphi)}X$ defined by $T\varphi := T\hat\varphi(x)$; $T\varphi$ can be defined for $\varphi$ on level at least $1$ and gives a bounded linear isomorphism on level $0$, and only for smooth $\varphi$ is $T\varphi$ an sc-operator. Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4) associates with a smooth morphism $\varphi$ the local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$ and its tangent $T\varphi$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V7.5, V8.12). With the linear structure of $T_xX$ (Definition 2.3.14; gap G.7 closed, V2.19), $T\varphi$ is a bounded linear isomorphism $T_{s(\varphi)}X \to T_{t(\varphi)}X$ with inverse $T(\varphi^{-1})$ for $\varphi \in \mathbf X_1$ (`tangentMorCLE`, `definition_7_1_4_linear`), and for smooth $\varphi$ an sc-isomorphism: in charts $T\varphi$ and $T(\varphi^{-1})$ are sc-operators restricting to mutually inverse maps of the sc-subspaces that are $T_{s(\varphi)}X$ and $T_{t(\varphi)}X$ as sc-Banach spaces (`definition_7_1_4_sc`, `tangentMor_chart_sc`, `Chapter7/TangentMorphismLinear.lean`). Earlier: `tangentMor` defines $T\varphi$; since 2026-11-07 (Chapter 8) it is well defined, $T\varphi(Ts(h)) = Tt(h)$ for every $h \in T_\varphi\mathbf X$ (`tangentMor_tSrc`), and functorial, $T(\psi \circ \varphi) = T\psi \circ T\varphi$ for $\varphi \in \mathbf X_1$ (`tangentMor_comp`), with the description of $T\mathbf X$ by the pairs $(T\varphi, a)$ of Remark 8.1.10 (2017: 8.1) (`remark_8_1_10`); since 2026-11-09, for $\varphi \in \mathbf X_1$, $T\varphi = T\hat\varphi(s(\varphi))$ (`tangentMor_eq_tangentMapOn_hat`), $T\varphi$ is a bijection $T_{s(\varphi)}X \to T_{t(\varphi)}X$ with inverse $T(\varphi^{-1})$ (`bijOn_tangentMor`), and in charts it is a bounded linear isomorphism of the tangent spaces of the retracts (`tangentMor_chart_iso`, `definition_7_1_4`). (Findings, Chapter 7, items 5, 110, 154; Chapter 8, item 112).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) and Proposition 7.10 (2017; rewritten in 2021 as Theorem 7.2.14): $\mathbf X^R$ Hausdorff and paracompact
notFormalized.label: §7.2, Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) and Proposition 7.10 (2017), pp. 313–324 (2017 pp. 242–244)
notFormalized.book: Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9): the reduced morphism set $\mathbf X^R$ has a natural M-polyfold structure. Proposition 7.10 (2017): every ep-groupoid $X$ possesses an associated reduced ep-groupoid $X_R$, and $X_R$ is effective. Since an M-polyfold is a paracompact Hausdorff space (Part I, Definition 2.3.4 (2017: 2.8)), these assert in particular that $\mathbf X^R$, with the quotient topology, is Hausdorff and paracompact, for every ep-groupoid $X$. The 2021 edition rewrites this: Remark 7.2.8 (p. 311) says that in general $(X, \mathbf X^R)$ cannot be made an ep-groupoid, Proposition 7.2.12 (p. 317) proves $T_R$ paracompact for every ep-groupoid, Proposition 7.2.13 (p. 318) makes it an M-polyfold exactly when it is Hausdorff, and Theorem 7.2.14 (p. 318) builds $X_R$ under the hypothesis that $T_R$ is Hausdorff, characterized in Theorem 7.2.22 (p. 323).
notFormalized.instead: **Closed by the 2021 edition**, in its 2021 form. In the 2017 form, for every ep-groupoid, the statement does not hold as we read it: for $\mathbb Z/2$ acting on the dimension-jumping retract of Part I's Remark 4.2.2 (2017: 4.3), $\mathbf X^R$ is not Hausdorff (`Examples.exists_not_t2Space_reducedMor`, formalized after the round-trip audit), and the hypotheses `[T2Space X.ReducedMor] [ParacompactSpace X.ReducedMor]` of `reducedPolyfold` were the project's (V7.39, V7.40). The 2021 text is consistent with this: Remark 7.2.8 announces such examples, Appendix 7.6.3 gives Zhou's, of the same kind (V7.82). Paracompactness is now proved for every ep-groupoid (`paracompactSpace_reducedMor`, an instance, V7.77), which also settles the question, left open here, of paracompactness when $\mathbf X^R$ is Hausdorff; the Hausdorff hypothesis is exactly that of 2021 Theorem 7.2.14 (V7.78), and Theorem 7.2.22 characterizes it by LUC and the closedness of $\mathbf X^T$ (V7.81) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 56, 60, 107, 111, 125, 126, 129).

notFormalized.title: The filtration of $|X|$: the set $|X_\infty|$
notFormalized.label: §7.1, 2017 p. 228
notFormalized.book: Since $ml(x) = ml(y) = ml(\varphi)$ for every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$, the filtration of $X$ induces the filtration $|X| = |X_0| \supset |X_1| \supset \dots \supset |X_\infty| = \bigcap_{k \ge 0} |X_k|$ of the orbit space $|X| = X/\sim$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V7.6). $|X_k| = \pi(X_k)$ is `orbitLevel k`, with $\pi^{-1}(|X_k|) = X_k$ (`preimage_orbitLevel`) and the filtration decreasing from $|X_0| = |X|$ (`orbitLevel_zero`, `orbitLevel_antitone`); $|X_\infty|$ is `orbitSmooth` $= \pi(X_\infty)$, and $|X_\infty| = \bigcap_k |X_k|$ (`orbitSmooth_eq_iInter`), since $X_k$ is saturated; `p290_orbit_filtration` bundles the filtration (Findings, Chapter 7, items 6, 112).

notFormalized.title: The density of $X_\infty$ in $X_k$
notFormalized.label: §7.1, 2017 p. 227
notFormalized.book: The M-polyfolds $X$ and $\mathbf X$ carry the filtrations $X = X_0 \supset X_1 \supset \dots \supset X_\infty = \bigcap_k X_k$; the set $X_\infty$ is dense in every space $X_k$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V7.6). For every M-polyfold $X$ and every $m$, $X_\infty$ is dense in $X_m$ (`MPolyfold.denseSmooth`): for a partial quadrant $C$, $C_m \cap E_\infty$ is dense in $C_m$ by the convexity of $C_m$ and its nonempty interior (`IsPartialQuadrant.lvlSet_subset_closure_smooth`), the same holds for $U$ relatively open in $C$, the fact used in the proof of Lemma 2.2.1 (`IsRelOpenInQuadrant.lvlSet_subset_closure_smooth`), and for a retract $O = r(U)$ by the continuity of $r$ on level $m$ (`IsScRetract.lvlSet_subset_closure_smooth`). For the object and the morphism M-polyfold of an ep-groupoid it is `p289_dense`, and Chapter 7's hypothesis `MPolyfold.DenseSmooth` (gap G.85) holds for every M-polyfold (Findings, Chapter 7, item 116).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 7.6.7: the sc-diffeomorphism $(X^i)_R \cong (X_R)^i$, and $i \ge 2$
notFormalized.label: §7.6, Theorem 7.6.7 and Corollary 7.6.8, p. 351 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: Under (SLUC), the natural set-theoretic identification between $(X^1)_R$ and $(X_R)^1$ is an sc-diffeomorphism between the object spaces and the morphism spaces; for every $i$ there is a similar identification between $(X^i)_R$ and $(X_R)^i$. Corollary 7.6.8: the same under (ZHOU).
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** beyond $i = 1$ as sets: under LUC for $X^1$ and the hypothesis that every $x \in X_1$ has a natural representation with $U(x) \cap X_1$ connected in $X^1$ and dense in $U(x)$ (the density is gap G.73), $(\mathbf X^1)^T = (\mathbf X^T)^1$ and $[\varphi]_1 \mapsto [\varphi]$ is a continuous injection $(\mathbf X^1)^R \to \mathbf X^R$ onto $\pi(\mathbf X_1)$ (V7.83). The sc-diffeomorphism needs the M-polyfold $(\mathbf X^R)^1$; $i \ge 2$ needs the lifts of $X_R$ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 131).

notFormalized.title: Appendix 7.6.3: Zhou's retract and its exact non-effective part
notFormalized.label: §7.6, Appendix 7.6.3, p. 348, and §7.4, p. 331 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: Zhou's example: $\mathbb Z/2$ acting on the retract of Part I's Subsection 1.4.4 by $(s, f) \mapsto (s, -f)$; $\mathrm{cl}(\mathbf X^T) \setminus \mathbf X^T$ is one point, so $T_R$ is not Hausdorff and (LUC) fails; the example does not satisfy the Zhou condition (p. 331).
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** for Zhou's retract: the analogue `JumpingRetract.X` ($\mathbb Z/2$ on the retract of Part I's Remark 4.2.2 (2017: 4.3)) has a point of $\mathrm{cl}(\mathbf X^T) \setminus \mathbf X^T$, $T_R$ not Hausdorff and LUC failing (V7.82); $\mathbf X^T$ is not computed exactly. That it fails (ZHOU) is proved, since 2026-11-09 with no hypothesis (`not_isZhou_unconditional`, V7.95) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 130, 139).

notFormalized.title: §7.4 for the index lifts $X^i$, $i \ge 2$: Propositions 7.4.9 and 7.4.18
notFormalized.label: §7.4, Proposition 7.4.9, p. 333, and Proposition 7.4.18, p. 336 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: Proposition 7.4.9: if $X$ satisfies the Zhou condition, so does every $X^i$ (the condition (ZHOU') being the same for $X$ and $X^i$). Proposition 7.4.18: (VSLUC) and (SLUC) are equivalent. Corollary 7.4.11, Theorems 7.4.13, 7.4.24 and Proposition 7.4.16 use them for every $X^i$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (Springer 2021 additions; V7.102–V7.104). The inclusions $X_{m+1} \to X_m$ are continuous and $(X^1)_\infty \to X_\infty$ is a homeomorphism; with Part I's Proposition 2.3.17 for $i = 1$ and the comparison of the natural representations of $X$ and $X^1$, (ZHOU') passes from $X$ to $X^1$, hence to every $X^i$, and Proposition 7.4.9 follows, with Corollary 7.4.11, Theorems 7.4.13 and 7.4.24 for (ZHOU) on $X$ only (V7.102). (VSLUC) and the density of $X_\infty$ pass from $X$ to every $X^i$, giving Propositions 7.4.16 and 7.4.17 (V7.103). Proposition 7.4.18 is proved in both directions, (SLUC) ⇒ (VSLUC) under natural representations with every $U(x) \cap X_m$ connected, which the text takes by construction (V7.104). Not formalized: (ZHOU') from $X^i$ back to $X$, which the proof does not use; the Part I facts stay hypotheses on every level (gap G.85) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 137, 148–150).

notFormalized.title: The Part I facts used in §7.4, and the connectedness of $U(x) \cap X_1$
notFormalized.label: §7.4, Lemma 7.4.4, p. 329, and the proofs of Lemma 7.4.6 to Proposition 7.4.22, pp. 331–340 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: The proofs use facts about M-polyfolds: $X_\infty$ dense in every $X_m$; $U(x) \cap X_\infty$ connected for connected open $U(x)$; tangent vectors approximated by tangent vectors at nearby smooth points; sc-smooth maps agreeing near a smooth point in $X_\infty$ have the same tangent there; $(T_xX)_\infty$ dense in $T_xX$. The proof of Lemma 7.4.4 uses that $U(x) \cap X_1$ is connected in $X^1$ and dense in $U(x)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V7.86, V7.83). Every fact is a theorem for every M-polyfold: `MPolyfold.smoothRegular` (from `denseSmooth`, gap G.73; `smoothConnected`, through smooth paths, `isPathConnected_smoothVal_preimage`; `isOpenMap_tangentProj`, gap G.8; `tangentDeterminedSmooth`) and `MPolyfold.denseSmoothTangent`. Every natural representation has $U(x) \cap X_1$ connected in $X^1$ and dense in $U(x)$ (`NaturalRep.isPreconnected_liftU`, `NaturalRep.subset_closure_inter_levelSet`), so `HasConnectedDenseLevelOneReps` holds for every ep-groupoid (`hasConnectedDenseLevelOneReps`), and so does `HasLevelOneConnectedDenseReps` of Lemma 7.4.4, which is not restated without it (V7.85); every natural representation has every $U(x) \cap X_m$ connected (`NaturalRep.levelConnected`), the text's \"by construction\" in Proposition 7.4.18. The §7.4, §7.6 and §8.1 results are restated without these hypotheses (V7.83, V7.89–V7.95, V7.102–V7.104, V8.45, V8.52) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 133, 134, 153).
